title: Hosted API — request salvage & tool contract heuristics
summary: Working draft that proposes a lightweight "request salvage" model for streaming Hosted API calls plus heuristics for tool-call contracts and SDK ergonomics to support resumable, idempotent client experiences. Focus is on pragmatic operator-friendly defaults and incremental rollouts.
background: As streaming + tool-calling surfaces proliferate, we keep hitting class of customer bugs where clients disconnect mid-stream or during a tool interaction and then reattach from a different device or ask for a replay. Current options are coarse: restart the whole request, or keep long-lived sessions that hold resources. We need a middle ground: allow safe "salvage" (resume + reconcile) without heavy server-side locking or burdening SDK ergonomics.
goals: 1) Define a minimal on-wire salvage protocol that works with streaming partial outputs and tool-call semantics. 2) Ensure tool-calls remain idempotent/observable and reconcilable when a client reconnects. 3) Provide SDK ergonomics that make resume/replay easy for app developers. 4) Tie salvage to observability and safety heuristics so operators can opt-in gradually.
non_goals: 1) Not attempting to replace full transactional tool orchestration or long-lived distributed sagas. 2) No heavy multi-region live-lock detection in the first phase. 3) Not a full spec for offline-first mobile; we aim to enable simpler offline replay patterns later.
product_requirements: - Every streaming request MAY include a client-supplied request-id and optional resume-token. - Server returns periodic commit checkpoints (incremental-commit markers) in the stream with compact metadata: checkpoint_id, sequence_offset, active_tool_calls. - Checkpoints are retained for a configurable resume-window (default 10 minutes for hosted, configurable for Dedicated). - Tool-calls expose a lightweight call-handle id and status states: pending, executing, completed, tombstoned. - Client reconnects can present last-seen checkpoint_id; server decides salvage path: fast-resume (continue from checkpoint), replay-from-checkpoint, or restart. - Operators can set salvage-policy per-customer: disabled / optimistic / conservative. - SDKs surface a single resume() API with clear callbacks for resumed-stream, missing-checkpoint, and reconcilation-conflict.
user_flows:
(A) Client disconnects mid-stream while model is generating and a tool call is pending: client reconnects within resume-window -> calls resume(last_checkpoint) -> SDK receives resumed-stream event with any buffered deltas and a tool-handle snapshot -> SDK rehydrates local UI, hooks into tool-handle to check tool result status (completed/needs-invocation) -> if tombstoned, SDK surfaces a consistent error and suggests user retry.

(B) Client reconnects after checkpoint retention expired: resume() returns missing-checkpoint -> SDK falls back to safe-restart flow: re-run request with best-effort dedupe and show user potential duplicate side-effects for explicit confirmation if tool action was side-effecting.

(C) Cross-device resume: same as (A) but client uses a different token; server applies policy to authorize resume only if request-id matches and customer policy allows cross-device.
protocol_spec:
High-level protocol sketch (non-normative):
- Client start: POST /v1/generate?request_id=<rid> body includes resume_policy (opt-in/adaptive) and client_metadata.
- Server streaming frames: {type: "delta" | "checkpoint" | "tool" | "end"} where checkpoint frame contains {checkpoint_id, seq_offset, active_tool_handles}. Delta frames are normal partial tokens/chunks. Tool frames emit tool-call-start(tool_handle, tool_name) and subsequent tool frames update tool_handle state.
- Resume: POST /v1/resume with {request_id, checkpoint_id, optional auth_token}. Server authenticates, checks retention window, and returns one of: {status: resumed, stream_cursor, tool_snapshots} or {status: missing_checkpoint, reason}.
- Tool-call idempotency: tool providers should implement a light dedupe key (tool_handle) + best-effort idempotent semantics. Where side-effects are unavoidable, UI must require explicit confirm on resume if tombstone/unknown result.
- Telemetry: every checkpoint emission increments checkpoint_counter metric; resume attempts emit resume_outcome enum (resumed|missing|conflict|denied).
sdk_surface:
Goals for SDK ergonomics: keep simple default, explicit opt-in for advanced flows.
- Primary surface: stream = client.createStream({requestId})
  stream.on('delta', cb), stream.on('checkpoint', cb), stream.on('tool', cb), stream.on('end', cb)
  stream.resume({checkpointId}).then({outcome})
- SDK automatically buffers last-seen checkpoint id and last token offset. If resume succeeds, SDK replays any buffered UI changes and invokes callbacks in consistent order.
- For tool-calls, SDK exposes ToolHandle objects with methods: status(), wait(), confirmSideEffect() and event hooks: on('complete'), on('tombstone').
- Mobile considerations: provide small persistent store adapter that keeps the last checkpoint metadata for cross-process resume but avoid storing full token buffers by default.
observability_and_metrics: Minimum signals: checkpoint_emitted{model,customer,route}, checkpoint_retention_eviction, resume_attempt{outcome}, resume_latency, tool_handle_state_transitions, duplicate_tool_invocation_detected. Logging: link resume attempts to trace ids; include checkpoint diffs in debug dumps (size-limited). Add a resume-rate SLO guard to avoid abuse.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (experiment): enable optimistic salvage for 5% of hosted API traffic on low-cost models; default retention 10 minutes. Instrument heavy telemetry. Phase 2 (beta): expose per-customer salvage-policy in console + increase rollout to 50% with configurable retention. Phase 3: GA with explicit Dedicated config and SLA guidance. Each phase includes a canary for tool-backed endpoints to ensure side-effects are visible and operators can disable salvage for those customers.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: accidental duplicated side-effects from resumed flows. Mitigation: tombstone tool handles after server-declared unsafe window; require explicit confirmSideEffect() by SDK for side-effecting results.\nRisk: storage/retention cost. Mitigation: default short retention window, tiered retention paid option.\nRisk: complexity for integrators. Mitigation: SDK hides most of the complexity; provide clear docs and sample UI patterns.
open_questions:
- Should checkpoint payloads be signed so cross-device resume can't be forged? (security trade-offs)
- What default retention is acceptable for enterprise vs hosted tiers?
- How to handle large tool outputs (binary attachments) in checkpoints — store pointers vs inline?
- Should we auto-invoke a lightweight verification probe on resume to detect model divergence?
next_steps: 1) Engineering spike: implement a minimal checkpoint emitter in runtime for one model (estimated 2 wks). 2) SDK spike: add resume() primitives and ToolHandle type (1 week). 3) Run tabletop with Solutions/CS: sample customer scenarios and decide default policies (this week). 4) Draft external developer guide and sample app showing cross-device resume and confirm flow (2 weeks).
notes_to_self: Keep the initial surface conservative: aim for good developer UX for read-heavy tool calls (e.g., lookups) and explicit guardrails for write-heavy tool calls. Coordinate with Security on resume auth model early.
